health_zone_table.basis: SitRep59 Table 2 (2026-07-12) transcribed + reconciled against the INSP final PDF (post 25143, media 25144, pdf sha256 73a0a4bdb74084f4d506fb538562a68596287b31ed30c0fe5aa2d2f10a0ea91e). Ituri's per-health-zone cumulative is the last consolidated distribution (10 July); the Ituri province total (1772/608) is the 12 July cumulative, and the gap is carried as unallocated residual (source-attribution lag, not smeared across zones). The three Tshopo/Kisangani detection communes (Makiso-Kisangani 2/2, Mangobo 1/0, Lubunga 1/0) are each mapped to their own distinct GRID3 v8.0 health-zone polygon (Kisangani) (4/2). No new health zone was notified on 12 July; the outbreak holds at 42 health zones across five provinces.

reconciliation.note: Named health-zone rows sum to 1876 confirmed / 684 confirmed deaths across all five provinces. Table 1 province totals are Ituri 1772/608, Nord-Kivu 177/100, Sud-Kivu 3/1, Haut-Uele 7/7, Tshopo 4/2 = national 1963/718. SR59 carries Ituri's per-zone distribution at the last consolidated cut (10 July): the named Ituri zone rows sum to 1689 confirmed / 578 deaths, so the province total (1772/608) leaves 17 explicitly unventilated Ituri cases plus a 66-confirmed / 30-death accumulated-since-distribution + DHIS2 reclassification residual. Nord-Kivu named rows sum to 173/96 vs its 177/100 province total (4-case lag). Haut-Uele Wamba is revised to 7/7 (all originating from Nia-Nia); Tshopo holds 4/2 (Makiso-Kisangani, Mangobo, Lubunga). Sud-Kivu holds 47+ consecutive days with no new confirmed case (last case 2026-05-26), residual-surveillance.

lab_indicators_24h.note: National aggregate: Ituri 203 analyzed / 27 positive (13.3%); Nord-Kivu 99 analyzed / 6 positive (6.1%); Sud-Kivu 8 collected and under analysis (excluded from positivity). Positivity uses 33 positives over 302 analyzed samples.

care_continuity: SitRep59 Tableau 5: 736 in isolation at end of day (246 confirmed / 490 suspected) at 88.3% global bed occupancy; Nord-Kivu 117.2% saturation, Ituri 82.1%, Sud-Kivu occupancy not reported this cut. Exits over 24h (108 total): 18 deaths, 65 non-cases, 15 recoveries, 9 escapes, 1 HGR transfer; 121 admissions. J-1 bed count 727.
Recovered advanced to 333 DRC cumulative (+15: Ituri 13, Nord-Kivu 2 at CTE Beni). The provincial-summed recovered (Ituri 317 + Nord-Kivu 27 = 344) is under national consolidation.
highlights: 31 new confirmed cases (Ituri 27, Nord-Kivu 4) and 10 deaths notified were reported for 2026-07-12; the 7 community deaths were all in Ituri (Bunia 3, Lita 2, Rwampara 1, Fataki 1) and the 3 Nord-Kivu deaths in Katwa (2) and Butembo (1). Confirmed cases rose to 1963 and deaths to 718; the global CFR is 36.6%.

No new health zone was notified on 12 July; the outbreak holds at 42 health zones across five provinces. Wamba (Haut-Uele) was revised to 7 confirmed / 7 deaths, all originating from Nia-Nia (Ituri); Tshopo/Kisangani holds 4 confirmed / 2 deaths (Makiso-Kisangani, Mangobo, Lubunga), all imported from the Nia-Nia/PK51 epicentre.

National isolation occupancy is 88.3% (736 patients: 246 confirmed, 490 suspected); Nord-Kivu remains saturated at 117.2% and Ituri at 82.1%. 15 patients were declared recovered (Ituri 13, Nord-Kivu 2), and 3 additional EDS teams were deployed to Nizi (6 total) against community mortality.

Ituri concentrates 27 of 31 new cases and all community deaths, at 1772 confirmed / 608 deaths (CFR 34.3%, ~90.5% of cases). Bunia (503), Rwampara (384), Mongbwalu (329), Nizi (110) and Nyankunde (97) remain the most affected; Mongbwalu shows the highest severity at 52.0%.

Nord-Kivu totals 177 confirmed / 100 deaths (CFR 56.5%), carried by Katwa (66.2%), Beni (66.7%) and Butembo (45.5%); the province retains a laboratory backlog and delayed diagnosis at 6.1% positivity.

Sud-Kivu has passed 47 consecutive days without a new confirmed case (last case 2026-05-26), holding in the residual-surveillance phase toward a provincial end-of-outbreak declaration; 17 patients remain in isolation.

alerts_total.data_gap_note: Tableau 3 (12 July): 46 carried (J-1) + 1110 new = 1156 alerts of the day across the four active provinces. Investigated 92.9% (Ituri 88.0%, Nord-Kivu 95.8%, Sud-Kivu 80.0%, Haut-Uele 96.9%). Validated suspects 268 = 156 living + 112 community deaths under investigation. Nord-Kivu concentrates 60.0% of alerts (694).

challenges.finding: Community reluctance toward post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs) and resistance delay confirmation, underestimate cases, and drive high community mortality.
challenges.response: Intensify RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, secure teams, and reinforce EDS teams (done: +3 in Nizi).

challenges.finding: Insufficient CTE/CT capacity with Nord-Kivu saturation at 117.2%; national isolation occupancy is 88.3% (736 patients), raising nosocomial-transmission risk.
challenges.response: Accelerate CTE expansion, deploy temporary structures, and open additional transit centres.

challenges.finding: Contact follow-up is under target (81.5% vs 95%) and heterogeneous (Nyankunde 28.9%, Nia-Nia 36.2%), leaving transmission chains uninterrupted.
challenges.response: Train, deploy, and motivate community relays (RECO) with reinforced supervision.

challenges.finding: Weak alert reporting and investigation in Ituri, with ZS/DHIS2 inconsistencies, risks undetected silent transmission.
challenges.response: Reinforce community-based surveillance, harmonize ZS/DHIS2 bases, and add investigators.

challenges.finding: None of the new confirmed cases were linked to a previously-listed contact (0% on 12 July), indicating uncontrolled community transmission.
challenges.response: Deepen investigation, active case-finding, and broaden contact listing.

challenges.finding: Insufficient ambulances and isolation structures delay transfer and isolation and raise transmission risk.
challenges.response: Preposition ambulances (including at PoE/PoC) and deploy transit centres in each health zone.

challenges.finding: A backlog of un-analyzed samples and late diagnosis persist in Nord-Kivu amid a 56.5% provincial CFR.
challenges.response: Deploy a laboratory catch-up plan and reinforce diagnostic capacity.

challenges.finding: Frontline personnel are heavily infected (114 confirmed cases, 36 deaths, CFR 31.6%), eroding capacity and raising nosocomial risk.
challenges.response: Reinforce IPC and supply PPE and IPC/EHA kits.

challenges.finding: Insecurity and limited access (Nia-Nia, CODECO/ADF) restrict operations in high-risk zones.
challenges.response: Strengthen security coordination and humanitarian access.

challenges.finding: High population mobility and urban extension toward Tshopo/Kisangani raise the risk of urban, riverine, and cross-border diffusion; 144094 travelers passed through PoE/PoC this cycle.
challenges.response: Reinforce PoE/PoC surveillance and cross-border/inter-provincial coordination.

challenges.finding: Insufficient resources constrain provider mobility and payment, demotivating responders.
challenges.response: Mobilize resources and regularize provider payments.

challenges.finding: Compromised continuity of essential (non-Ebola) health services, with insufficient MEG and nutritional inputs, raises indirect mortality.
challenges.response: Make free care effective and procure essential medicines and nutritional inputs.

contacts_total.data_gap_note: Tableau 4 (12 July): 12370 under follow-up, 10156 seen, 82.1%. Ituri 79.4% (9866/7830), Nord-Kivu 90.5% (2377/2152). New contacts listed: Ituri 405, Nord-Kivu 164; 8 became suspect in Ituri (12 in Nord-Kivu); 364 completed 21-day follow-up. Sud-Kivu narrative reports 226 contacts under follow-up (2 became positive), not included in the Tableau-4 total. The cover KPI shows 81.5% aggregate; the internally consistent Tableau-4 total 82.1% is promoted. 0 of 27 new Ituri confirmed were previously-listed contacts.

patient_movement_total.data_gap_note: SitRep59 Tableau 5 end-of-day census 736 at 88.3% occupancy (Ituri 549 @82.1%, Nord-Kivu 170 @117.2%, Sud-Kivu 17 occupancy n.d.). The dont-rows (246 confirmed + 490 suspected) sum exactly to the 736 census this cycle. J-1 bed count 727. Exits (108 total): 18 deaths, 65 non-cases, 15 recoveries, 9 escapes, 1 HGR transfer; 121 admissions (Ituri 85, Nord-Kivu 12, Sud-Kivu 24). Two suspected cases left Ituri isolation before their result.

priorities.priority: Resolve the 17 unventilated Ituri confirmed cases and the 66-case / 30-death Ituri distribution lag (per-zone cut 10 July vs 12 July province total) without smearing them across named health zones; confirm the Wamba revision (7/7) and the Tshopo/Kisangani accounting (4/2).
Relieve isolation load at 88.3% national occupancy and Nord-Kivu 117.2% saturation (56.5% provincial CFR); accelerate CTE construction/expansion and additional transit centres.
Improve contact follow-up (82.1% vs 95% target), raise Ituri alert investigation above 88.0%, and clear the Nord-Kivu laboratory backlog / delayed diagnosis.
Sustain residual epidemiological surveillance in Sud-Kivu (47+ days with no new confirmed case) toward a provincial end-of-outbreak declaration, while resolving the 17 patients still in isolation.

preserved_conflicts: SitRep59 national headline is DRC-only (1963 confirmed / 718 confirmed deaths across five provinces); the country-scope snapshot adds the Uganda component (20/2/11) separately -> 1983 confirmed / 720 deaths / 344 recovered.

Confirmed-death total conflict: the SR59 cover KPI card displays 719 deaths, but the CFR footnote computes 718/1963 = 36.6%, the page-1 narrative states 718, and the Table-1 province total is 718. The internally consistent 718 is promoted and the 719 cover KPI is flagged inconsistent.

Tshopo deaths conflict: SR59 Table-1 prints Tshopo 4/3 (and the cover KPI totals 719), while the page-1 narrative states Tshopo 4 cases / 2 deaths and the CFR footnote uses 718/1963. The named Tshopo health-zone rows (Makiso-Kisangani 2 + Mangobo 0 + Lubunga 0) sum to 2 deaths; promoting Tshopo = 2 keeps the national total internally consistent at 718.

Per-zone distribution lag: SR59 Table 2 carries Ituri's per-health-zone cumulative at the last consolidated distribution (10 July), while the Ituri province total (1772/608) is the 12 July cumulative. The named Ituri zone rows sum to 1689 confirmed / 578 deaths, so beyond the 17 explicitly unventilated cases a 66-confirmed / 30-death accumulated-since-distribution + DHIS2 reclassification residual is carried as unallocated (not smeared across zones per the source-load policy). Nord-Kivu shows a smaller 4-case lag (province 177 vs named 173). Several zone markers (Bunia 507->503, Nizi 121->110) legitimately decrease vs SR58 as the source reverted to the 10 July consolidated distribution.

Recovered instability: the SR59 cover cumulative is 333 (= 318 + 15 recoveries: Ituri 13, Nord-Kivu 2), while the provincial-summed recovered is Ituri 317 + Nord-Kivu 27 = 344, with national consolidation in progress. The cover cumulative 333 (DRC) / 344 (country-scope, +11 Uganda) is promoted; the provincial 344 is preserved as the unstable alternative.
Contact follow-up conflict: the SR59 cover shows 81.5% aggregate while Tableau 4 totals 82.1% (10156/12370; Ituri 79.4%, Nord-Kivu 90.5%). The internally consistent Tableau-4 total 82.1% is promoted.
Sud-Kivu has passed 47 consecutive days with no new confirmed case (last case 2026-05-26), in the residual-surveillance phase toward a provincial end-of-outbreak declaration.
